At 1KOMMA5° , we pursue a clear vision: Living on wind and sunlight forever for free . To make this a reality, we are building the energy system of the future with Heartbeat AI. Want to be part of it?
We bring together regional craftsmanship and scalable software: We don't think of solar, batteries, heat pumps, and e-mobility as isolated components, but control them as an intelligent, integrated overall system in our virtual power plant. Directly connected to the electricity market – in real time, fully automated.

This way, energy is used when it is available from renewables and particularly cost-effective. By 2030, our goal is to transition 1.5 million households to renewable energies. Over 3,000 people are working towards this every day, at more than 80 locations worldwide, from Finland to Australia.
Want to take responsibility and build solutions that truly matter? Apply now and help us shape the energy world of tomorrow.
Learn about our Product & Tech team!
Deine Position
As Product Manager Procurement & Portfolio Management, you take on one of the most strategically defining product roles within our energy retail business: you design how 1KOMMA5° procures, hedges, and optimizes electricity for an increasingly flexible customer portfolio. You sit at the intersection of energy markets, energy procurement, our flexibility assets, and our customer-facing tariff strategy - and you turn this into a measurable commercial advantage.
Own our Procurement Strategy: Define how and where 1KOMMA5° procures energy for our customer portfolio - across day-ahead, intraday, and forward markets. Develop a clear market split logic, and continuously refine it based on portfolio characteristics, customer mix, and market conditions.
Design Portfolio Hedging & Risk Management: Build hedging and risk management strategies tailored to different customer portfolios (dynamic vs fixed tariffs or flexibility/ancillary services). Define when and how we lock in volumes, what we leave open, and how we balance commercial upside against risk exposure.
Shape Our Flexibility Procurement Model: Design how we procure and steer our flexibility portfolio. Defining models such as flexibility bands, fixed volumes, strike-price-based offers, and the trade-offs between them. Develop the commercial logic and the operational requirements for each model.
Run Quantitative Portfolio Analysis: Independently run analyses on procurement performance, hedging effectiveness, and portfolio economics. Build the analytical foundation that supports strategic decisions, identifies optimization opportunities, and quantifies the impact of changes to our procurement and steering setup.
Monitor Performance and Drive Continuous Improvement: Define KPIs across procurement cost, hedge effectiveness, portfolio risk, and flexibility margin. Use data to continuously sharpen our market positioning and commercial performance.
Dein Profil

4+ years of experience in (international) energy procurement, portfolio management, or energy trading, ideally in a utility, energy retailer, trading desk, or aggregator environment
Strong analytical skills with hands-on experience running portfolio analyses, hedge calculations, and market scenarios (Python, SQL, or comparable tools are a strong plus)
Proven ability to translate market and commercial logic into structured processes and product requirements
Entrepreneurial, proactive, and comfortable navigating ambiguity in a fast-moving market environment
Excellent written and spoken English and German

Deep understanding of European power markets - day-ahead, intraday, and forward markets - and the mechanisms that drive prices
Solid working knowledge of hedging instruments (futures, options, OTC), balancing markets, and BRP settlement
Familiarity with flexibility products and procurement models (flexibility bands, fixed volumes, strike-price offers) and their commercial trade-offs
Awareness of regulatory frameworks shaping energy retail (Marktkommunikationsprozesse, balancing regimes, market design developments)
Experience working with external procurement partners, ETRM systems, or trading platforms is a strong plus

You are part of an international, dynamic, and highly motivated team of people who have proven to make things happen
With your work, you accelerate the "energy transition" and hence have a direct impact on our climate
Work with and learn from other super-smart colleagues
You will enjoy direct contact with core decision-makers
You will enjoy the best chances of entering full-time in one of Europe's most thriving scaleups
You can work in one of our offices in Hamburg, Berlin or Munich
Create a healthy balance alongside your work and enjoy all the benefits of the EGYM Wellpass

In this role, you will envision and deliver a multi-gig experience that is intuitive, fast, globally scalable and tailored to different earner segments. We achieve this through optimizing the onboarding experience, enabling earners to progress during their early lifecycle and by helping to maximize their earning potential through multiple gigs to increase retention. In the event that earners churn, we also focus on bringing them back to the platform.

Own the product roadmap and lead vision, definition and execution for building Uber's earner multi gig experience.
Rethink the journey - deeply understand earners, their motivations and challenges and keep making the gig discovery and recommendation experience better.
Innovate - find new ways of simplifying the user experience with new technologies.
Distill vision and strategy for the team, get all members of cross-functional team #superpumped.
Own your numbers, drive your cross-functional team of engineers, data scientist, product ops and designers to set qualitative objectives and quantitative goals -- and overachieve them.
Clearly communicate product plans, benefits, and results to leadership.

Minimum of 6 years of product management experience.
Experience delivering highly successful and creative consumer Internet products with your fingerprints all over them - you're proud of what you've accomplished.
Data-driven: you always get the data you need, and you can distill it into an insightful story. Most importantly, you leverage data to drive strategic decisions.
Technical skills. Ability to inform and evaluate engineering decisions.

Any experience working with gig economy earners
Launching products in different international markets

We are building a SaaS platform that packages Autodesk Consulting’s intellectual property — proven workflows, implementation guidance, learning content, and tooling recommendations — into a scalable digital experience that connects customers and internal Autodesk consultants to the knowledge they need to drive successful digital transformation. This is a platform built at the intersection of knowledge management, content delivery, and AI-assisted discovery, and it is evolving rapidly.
As Senior Principal Product Manager, you will own the full platform — the foundation on which our Solutions, Services, and advisory experiences are built.

You will define and drive the product vision and roadmap, work directly with lead architects and engineering teams across India and Poland, partner closely with our UI/UX designer, and collaborate with Product Owners who manage sprint-level delivery across multiple scrum teams.

You will also serve as the connective tissue between three critical stakeholder groups: the customers and Autodesk consultants who use the platform daily, and the Solutions and Services PMs who have a stake in how their content and services are experienced and consumed.
This is a role for someone who is energized by building. The platform is new, the market opportunity is significant, and the roadmap reflects that ambition. The person in this role will thrive on creating structure in a fast-moving environment, making high-quality decisions with incomplete information, and shaping a product that is still defining what it can become.

Own the end-to-end product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the platform, balancing near-term delivery with long-term platform integrity
Define and drive the AI-assisted discovery and personalization strategy that enables customers and consultants to find relevant workflows, solutions, and knowledge based on their specific context
Partner with lead architects and senior engineers across globally distributed teams to translate product strategy into technical direction
Work with Product Owners to ensure roadmap priorities are effectively executed across multiple scrum teams
Collaborate with Solutions and Services PMs to ensure platform capabilities effectively support content delivery and service consumption experiences
Develop deep understanding of the needs of both external customers and internal Autodesk consultants, and translate those needs into platform features and experiences
Define and track success metrics that reflect both platform health and the business outcomes the platform is designed to drive
Navigate a complex stakeholder environment, building alignment across consulting leadership, engineering, design, and go-to-market teams
Contribute to the commercialization strategy, helping define how the platform creates and captures value over time

10+ years of product management experience, with a track record of shipping complex, multi-stakeholder products
Demonstrated experience building AI-enabled applications, particularly in the areas of intelligent search, contextual discovery, recommendation systems, or personalization
Experience building products that span SaaS applications, content platforms, and service delivery — not just traditional software features
Proven ability to operate effectively in early-stage or rapidly evolving product environments where structure and clarity must be created, not inherited
Strong technical fluency, with the ability to engage meaningfully with architects and engineers on system design, data architecture, and AI/ML approaches
Experience working with globally distributed engineering teams
Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence without authority at a senior level
Nice to have: experience building content lifecycle management products, particularly those involving structured, hierarchical, or reusable content — including authoring, publishing workflows, versioning, and change propagation
AI/ML frameworks and application patterns, including RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), vector databases, semantic search, and large language model integration
Modern SaaS platform architecture and API-driven product design
Content management and knowledge management systems
Content lifecycle management tooling, including structured authoring environments, library management, and publishing workflows
Analytics and data pipeline tooling
Agile delivery methodologies and experience working with Product Owners across multiple scrum teams
The Ideal Candidate
The ideal candidate has built products where an intelligent discovery layer is the differentiator — where the ability to surface the right knowledge, in the right context, for the right user is what makes the product worth using. They understand what it takes to make that experience feel effortless, and they bring the technical depth to engage meaningfully with engineers and architects on how to build it.
They are comfortable in the ambiguity of a brand new product. They don’t need a mature backlog or a well-worn playbook — they can create structure where none exists, make sound decisions with incomplete information, and keep a complex roadmap moving without losing sight of the long-term vision.
They think in systems. They understand that a platform serving customers, internal consultants, and peer product managers simultaneously requires architectural thinking, not just feature thinking.
They are a natural connector. In a role that sits at the center of platform, solutions, and services, they build trust quickly, communicate with clarity, and have a track record of aligning diverse stakeholders around a shared direction.
A candidate who also brings experience with content lifecycle management — structured authoring, library systems, versioning, and hierarchical content relationships — would bring a rare and particularly valuable perspective to this role.

We are building the world's decision infrastructure: the strategic twin of every industrial organization for complex combinatorial problems. We unlocked what wasn't possible before: mapping reality with its levers and constraints into a computer, then running n-dimensional optimization on critical value-chain decisions. We help Europe stay strong and the German Mittelstand make good decisions between market shifts, orders, machines and people.
Founded by Dana (CEO) and Erik (CTO) from RWTH research, backed by a €2.8M round led by Vorwerk Ventures, with customers live on our optimization models.
We move fast. We care. No patience for problems left unsolved.

You own the product and the priorities behind it. The hard part of that job here is structural: our go-to-market runs vertically, one use case at a time, while the product has to stay general enough to serve the next customer without being rebuilt.
You sit between Sales and Engineering and translate in both directions. Towards Sales: which use cases we can sell today, which we cannot, and what a demo is allowed to claim. Towards Engineering: which requirement is ready to be built, what it needs to be complete, and what we deliberately leave out.
This is an early-stage role and we expect you to shape it rather than inherit it. We are extending the core of the application right now, which means your first decisions land while the product is still taking form. At the beginning, a meaningful part of your work will be spent on customer projects, close to the people whose decisions we model. That is where you see which patterns are worth turning into product.
We will not sugarcoat it: short deadlines, wild workload, and a go to market with the product and its tech that is a day to day focus and iteration process.
What you'll own
The product roadmap and the reasoning behind it: what we build next, in which order, and what we decline.
The boundary between standard product, configuration, and manual work for one customer.
Requirements that engineering can build from: scope, acceptance criteria, and a clear statement of what is out.
What we can credibly promise a customer, including where the product's limits currently are.
Proofs of Value that you run yourself, and responsibility for individual accounts.
Prototypes you build to test features with customers before we commit engineering time.
How product works here: discovery, prioritisation, and the standards between product and engineering.
Your number: how much of what is project work today is standard product a year from now, and the time from a recognised customer problem to a usable capability.
This role is not for you if your strength is backlog, process and ceremonies, if you need research and design capacity before you can decide, if a complex industrial domain is an obstacle rather than the interesting part, if you don't like data or if you need more than three days before your first customer conversation.

A technical and analytical foundation, engineering, data analytics, data science, operations research, quantitative controlling, or finance with real modelling from a technical degree, technical consulting, or technical product management. You will not write production code, but you need to recognise when a requirement creates technical debt, or is built in a way that cannot be reused at the next customer.
5+ years in product management, or consulting with genuine product proximity. More important than the title: you have owned a product area end to end before, not only a backlog.
Experience deciding under incomplete information, and the ability to explain your trade-offs afterwards: what you chose, why, and what it cost.
You can sit with a plant manager or a controller, understand how they decide today, and leave the room knowing what the product has to do about it.
Good to have, not a cut off: optimization experience, deeper knowledge in manufacturing, supply chain or S&OP, enterprise B2B sales cycles involving operations, IT and controlling, or early-stage startup experience.
German C1 or higher, fluent in English.
NRW-based (Cologne office), optionally Munich, Stuttgart, Berlin area or else willing to work hybrid. Open to find a way if we fit.

Impact. You work with substance and lead what the product becomes.
Ownership. You define how product works here: what we build, what we decline, and where the boundary between product and project sits. No approval loops.
The people next to you. You work directly with the researchers and modellers, have access to tech deliveries and execute and build on eye level with the founders.
Exposure. You present your own roadmap and the reasoning behind it to the board, you sit in the core strategy conversations, and you stand in front of the people whose decisions we model.
Feedback speed. You will know directly what you are up to, we speak out loud, we adjust, we grow. Together.
High stakes. Competitive salary and relevant room in the equity package (VSOP) to match your contribution and your career development.
Process: Intro call with Dana or Erik, second call with one from the team, a 60 to 90-minute live case exercise on a real customer requirement, then team conversations in person. Before you decide, ask us to put you on a call with someone who will tell you the good, the bad and the ugly.
"Hustle the day, analyse at night, reinforce something outstanding." Period.

Tasks

Translate customer conversations, user feedback, product data, regulatory requirements, and company goals into clear product decisions.

You independently drive your roadmap, make difficult prioritisation decisions, and demonstrate measurable impact. Your understanding of customers begins to shape Parto's broader product strategy.

Product Manager: Alternative Payment Processing
Checkout.com is seeking a Product Manager and leader to join our team of product managers working to add and improve our Alternative Payment Method (APM) portfolio, with a focus on bank-based payment rails.

This role will help drive our company OKR of expanding and enhancing the payment methods we offer merchants around the world, helping these businesses grow their global footprint.

The successful candidate will provide cross-functional leadership across product, engineering, and business teams, to ensure our APM portfolio is embedded throughout Checkout.com ’s ecosystem, enabling a seamless experience for our merchants.

They will work across the business and engage with merchants to align on the selection of APMs, drive the recommended approach to offer or improve them, design the API experience and collaborate with more than twenty stakeholder teams to deliver APMs end-to-end.

Daily tasks include understanding stakeholders’ pain points, driving prioritization for product development, and developing new capabilities for our customers.

3-5 years of product management experience.
Experience working in payment methods, especially direct debit and account-to-account payment methods
Data-driven: Skilled at leveraging data and business insights to determine strategic priorities and drive the product roadmap and execution.
Customer-first: Think from the customer's perspective and can balance future opportunities with immediate needs.
End-to-end mindset: Think in a structured and diligent manner, understanding all key components necessary to drive the ongoing success of a product.
Leadership: Excellent at collaborating with stakeholders in product, engineering, commercial, and business teams proactively, demonstrating high EQ and influencing skills.
Effective communicator: Able to inspire others with a shared vision and simplify complex concepts for a wide range of audiences.

Set the strategy for your portfolio of APMs, including understanding the target market, customers and aims for each APM, to determine the best approach for delivering the APMs, and how to balance adding new APMs vs working on enhancements for the existing portfolio, using qualitative and quantitative research and data to make decisions.
Become an expert in your payment methods, working closely with the payment partners to understand trends and drivers for success, which you will leverage to support our commercial team and drive value for our merchants.
Work with engineering and product counterparts to design the API and integration for each APM, to deliver an optimal developer experience which balances a consistent API experience across Checkout.com ’s products with the nuances of each different APM.
Build strong partnerships with business, product, and technology stakeholders and work with them for their buy-in and collaboration to generate momentum for your products
Work with other product and engineering leaders to ensure alignment with their roadmaps and delivery
Gain a deep understanding of Checkout.com ’s customers and business.
Foster a team culture that upholds Checkout.com ’s operating principles.

At Cheesecake Labs , product work usually starts before things are fully defined.

That’s why we maintain a network of strong contractor Product Managers we can engage quickly as new projects and client opportunities emerge.

It’s a contractor opportunity designed for people who enjoy navigating ambiguity, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, and helping turn business problems into valuable digital products across different industries and client contexts.

Contractor / project-based engagement
Paid in USD
Remote-first
Flexible allocation depending on project availability and fit
Opportunities may vary in duration, scope, and weekly commitment depending on client needs

What this role actually looks like
This is not a “just manage backlog” type of role.

s.h: On a typical project, you might
s.t:
Work with clients and stakeholders to understand business goals, user problems, and product opportunities
Help shape product direction even when requirements, priorities, or product vision are still evolving
Create and organize product backlogs, user stories, business rules, and feature definitions
Work closely with delivery managers, designers, and engineers to define valuable, feasible, and usable solutions
Facilitate alignment across clients, technical teams, and business stakeholders
Participate in product discovery, roadmap discussions, prioritization, and go-to-market conversations

We’ve seen that people who thrive in this type of engagement usually:
Have strong experience managing digital products across web and mobile environments
Feel comfortable navigating ambiguity, evolving priorities, and fast-changing product contexts
Know how to balance business goals, user needs, technical constraints, and delivery realities
Feel totally confident working in English with international clients and teams (calls, discussions, async) — at least advanced level
Operate well across multidisciplinary environments involving product, engineering, design, and delivery teams

Already use AI as part of their day-to-day workflow — whether for organization, discovery, documentation, research, prioritization, or workflow acceleration
Previous experience in consulting/service environments, enterprise products, or US-based client contexts is a strong plus.

You prefer highly structured environments with very stable scopes and long planning cycles
You’re uncomfortable navigating ambiguity or balancing multiple stakeholders and priorities simultaneously
You prefer operating only at a strategic level without involvement in execution and day-to-day product decisions
You’d rather avoid client-facing conversations or cross-functional collaboration
You rely heavily on mature product structures, large internal product teams, or extensive metrics environments to operate effectively
There’s nothing wrong with any of that — it’s just not how these engagements usually operate.

As a Senior Product Manager, you own whether the solution is valuable to customers and viable for the business, working alongside design and engineering, who bring usability and feasibility. This role needs to build strong working relationships across design and engineering and pull in the right partners for the problem at hand.

It also needs a working knowledge of the constraints across marketing, sales, customer success, finance, accounting, legal, and privacy, plus a deep understanding of who our athletes are and how they actually use our products.

That depth comes from genuine curiosity: about the business, about the families and athletes we serve, about the data behind their behavior, and about the technology, including AI, that shapes what's possible for the product.

The best person for this this role builds shared context across the teams around them, and earns trust and rapport with stakeholders, not through authority, but by consistently showing up with the right questions and the right evidence. This role sits at the bleeding edge of solving problems for families navigating the college recruiting process.

The decisions made here will shape the experience for thousands of families, and in some cases change the course of a young athlete's life. It's an individual contributor role, accountable for solving real problems for customers in a way that works for the business, not just shipping a list of features.

Success here is measured by the outcomes we create for athletes and families, and by how those outcomes move the business forward.

Execute against and help inform the product vision and strategy for the Core Athlete experience, translating it into a roadmap where each phase of work builds on the one before it, not just a queue of features. Foster shared understanding of that vision and strategy across your team and stakeholders.
Build and maintain deep, current knowledge of the business, our athletes and families, the data behind their behavior, and the technology behind our products, and use that knowledge to spot the right problems early.
Own the backlog. Write user stories and acceptance criteria that make the “why” clear, not just the “what.”
Partner with design and engineering, and pull in the right people across the business, to move from discovery to delivery.
Run experiments to test solutions before betting the roadmap on them. Feasibility and usability get tested early, not discovered late.
Track industry trends and the competitive landscape in athlete recruiting, and bring that context back to the team.
Stay fluent in AI as it evolves. Spot where it can change the product for athletes and families, and use it to speed up your own research, analysis, and daily workflow.
Build trust and rapport with stakeholders across Marketing, Sales, Operations, and Support. Use data and a clear narrative, not just authority, to align people around decisions.
Stay accountable for the metrics behind the roadmap, not just the delivery schedule.

5+ years of product management experience, ideally including consumer-facing or user-facing products on a sprint-based, cross-functional team.
Demonstrated ability to run product discovery: framing problems, testing solutions with real users, and killing ideas that don't hold up.
Working SQL skills. You should be comfortable pulling and interpreting your own data rather than waiting on someone else's report.
Experience partnering directly with engineers and designers as peers to move ideas from discovery to delivery.
Genuine curiosity about the business, the customer, the data, and the technology, and the judgment to know which one matters most for a given problem.
AI fluency: comfortable using AI tools day to day, and sharp enough about what AI can and can't do to spot where it genuinely changes the product.
A track record of turning ambiguous, cross-functional problems into a clear, prioritized backlog.
Proven track record of translating complex business needs into clear product strategies and roadmaps.
Exceptional communication and storytelling skills. You should be able to write a one-page narrative that convinces a skeptical exec, and influence and align senior stakeholders, not just present a slide deck that restates numbers.
Highly self-motivated and resourceful, comfortable leading both strategy and execution.
Experience working in Agile/Scrum development environments.
Comfortable holding a position and defending it with data, while staying genuinely open to being wrong.

An Introduction to Primer
Primer is the unified infrastructure for global payments. We give finance and payments teams the visibility and control to reduce complexity, improve performance, and capture more revenue - all from a single platform.
Backed by Sofina, Peak XV Partners, ICONIQ, Tencent, Accel, and Balderton, we're building the payments layer the world's best companies rely on.
Watch our showcase >
Read up on our $100m Series C

Which team will you be joining?
Getting paid is only half the story. Understanding and managing those payments is where the real work begins.
In the Financial Operations team we build the tools and infrastructure that let merchants take control of their payments: reconciling funds, monitoring performance, and automating the operations that keep everything running. We also own Global Accounts, giving merchants the ability to hold, manage and move funds across currencies and markets, a foundational capability as Primer expands into more complex, cross-border payment environments.
The team spans Reconciliation, Operations Automation, Global Accounts and FX. As a Product Manager here you will own a sub-area within that: a coherent slice of the product where you own the problems, the prioritisation and the outcomes over multiple quarters.
You will work day to day with a dedicated engineering team and design partner, alongside GTM, and report into the Product lead for the area. Primer is remote-first and globally distributed, and always will be. We run on written thinking, low bureaucracy and real ownership. You build it, you own it, end to end.
What will you be doing?
Owning the outcomes for your sub-area of Financial Operations over multiple quarters, not just shipping a backlog
Defining the problems worth solving in your scope by synthesising merchant feedback, support data, competitive moves and platform constraints
Planning and delivering initiatives independently, making real-time trade-offs on scope, sequencing and quality to protect both timelines and outcomes
Writing specs that anticipate the edge cases that actually matter in payments operations: reconciliation breaks, currency and settlement complexity
Partnering closely with engineering on feasibility and technical trade-offs, and defining the leading and lagging metrics that tell you whether your sub-area is working
Owning launch readiness and driving rapid post-launch iteration based on what the data shows
Representing your sub-area to merchants and internal stakeholders, turning operational complexity into clear product decisions

A track record of owning a product sub-area or significant feature set end to end, with outcomes that can be traced back to your decisions
The ability to define problems independently from messy inputs, rather than waiting for a fully formed brief
Sound, autonomous trade-offs on scope, quality and technical debt within your scope
Enough technical fluency to partner with engineers on feasibility and integration implications, not just hand over requirements
Clear, structured communication that keeps engineering, design and GTM aligned and surfaces risks early

Experience in payments, fintech, or operational and back-office product such as reconciliation, ledgers, treasury or FX
Comfort with data analysis to define and track outcome metrics
You may not like it here
Financial operations is detail-heavy and unforgiving. Reconciliation and FX have real money and real edge cases attached. If you prefer broad, abstract product work to getting the details exactly right, this will frustrate you.
You are expected to define what is worth solving in your sub-area, with support rather than direction.
We are remote-first and async by default. If you need people physically around you to do your best work, this is a real adjustment, not a perk.
Feedback here is direct and frequent. You are expected to give it as well as take it.

TL;DR — alago brings AI-powered project management to the construction industry. As our Product Manager , you'll own a core product area end to end: how messy project data becomes an early warning that a €200M project is about to go wrong. Full-time, Munich.
About alago
Imagine if building a building were as easy as building software. Every moving part visible, every change traceable, every decision still carrying its reasoning six months later.
Software got there by making its own history legible — every commit, every diff. Construction never did. A €200M project runs on plan sets nobody can diff and decisions buried in email, so the same mistakes happen over and over, and the industry loses $1.6 trillion a year to it.
That's what we're fixing. Eleven people, 15+ customers, €1M+ pre-seed from leading construction-tech VCs and one of Germany's largest project developers. The product is live and used daily on real construction sites — which means the interesting work is only starting.
Tasks

Translate deeply technical construction workflows into decisions engineers can build from
Own a product area end to end: From discovery on site to shipped, instrumented, measured features
Shape the roadmap: Balance what the next customer needs against the foundations that make the next ten cheap
Make the hard prioritization calls on scope and sequencing, and defend them
Define what "working" means: pick the metrics, instrument them, read production data, iterate
Treat LLM behavior as a product problem, not a research one — evals, fallbacks, and what the user sees when the model is wrong

Must-haves
2+ years shipping product — as a product manager, or as a UI/product designer who's been making product calls and not just screens
You've shipped something where the hard part was the data model, not the button
Hands-on experience with LLM-powered features in production — you know what breaks and how users react when it does
Genuine willingness to put on boots and go on site until you know the domain better than we do
Bonus
AEC background
Founder experience, or product work at a company under 20 people
You already build your own agents and internal tools to do your job faster
Not a match on every line? Apply anyway — potential and learning curve count.

You'll be one of our first product hires, which means you own critical parts of the product end to end and work directly with the founders. It's early enough that you help decide how the company works, and the path from here goes to either top individual contributor or leading product as we grow, depending on where you're strongest.

Hybrid: three days a week in our central Munich office (WERK1).
Plus: Wellpass, team dinners twice a week, relocation support.

1. Submit your story
Tell us about something you built that had real impact.

Intro, Logistics & Fit with a founder.
3. Product Challenge (45min)
Tackle a product challenge in person

We’ll get back to you within 24 hours. If it’s a fit — let’s go! 🎉

As the Staff Product Manager for OpenTelemetry Experience, you’ll own the end-to-end journey for helping people and agents instrument workloads and successfully send useful OpenTelemetry data to Grafana Cloud.
Your mission is to make Grafana Cloud the easiest and most trusted destination for OpenTelemetry workloads. You’ll reduce the uncertainty, complexity, and failure points users encounter between deciding to adopt OpenTelemetry and receiving healthy, correctly attributed, and actionable telemetry in Grafana Cloud.
Teams can instrument workloads, directly or with the help of coding agents, through OpenTelemetry SDKs, automatic instrumentation technologies such as Beyla and SDK injection, or client-side OpenTelemetry Collectors. Each path presents different decisions, deployment requirements, configuration steps, and potential failure modes.

You’ll define a coherent experience that helps users choose the right approach, complete setup successfully, troubleshoot problems, and understand whether their telemetry is healthy and useful. You’ll design a future in which a growing share of instrumentation work is performed by coding agents acting on behalf of developers.

This means treating agents are first-class participants in the experience and ensuring that instrumentation options, configuration requirements, errors, and validation signals are structured, discoverable, and actionable by both humans and machines.

Automatic instrumentation experiences, including OBI/Beyla and SDK injection

Collector configuration, authentication, and initial connectivity
Guidance and machine-readable context that help people and agents choose the right instrumentation approach
Workflows that allow coding-agents to implement, configure and verify instrumentation safely
Troubleshooting missing, incomplete, malformed, or unhealthy telemetry
Validation signals that allow both people and agents to confirm that telemetry is healthy, correctly attributed, and usable in Grafana Cloud
The transition from receiving telemetry to activating the appropriate Grafana Cloud observability solution

You’ll partner closely with teams responsible for experiences such as Application Observability, Kubernetes Monitoring, Infrastructure Observability, and Drilldown Apps to ensure OpenTelemetry workloads receive a first-class experience from initial setup through first value.
This is a horizontal Staff-level product leadership role spanning multiple products and engineering teams. You’ll model thoughtful, hands-on adoption of AI while applying strong judgement to its outputs.
The role is not focused on developing OpenTelemetry as an open source project in isolation. You’ll engage with and contribute to the OpenTelemetry ecosystem where appropriate, while measuring success through customer activation and outcomes in Grafana Cloud.

Solid products are built on a clear knowledge of real customer needs. In large enterprise accounts, those needs arrive as a constant stream of enhancement requests, feature asks, and hard problems.

In this high-impact role, you will own the relationship between Elastic Security's product organization and our most strategic enterprise accounts. You will manage enhancement requests across many enterprise customers at once.

You will prioritize them with judgment and data, and make sure they keep transitioning through the system instead of sitting idle.

You will be the person a CISO trusts in the room, the person an engineering lead respects for the quality of your requirements, and the person who can tell a major customer that something will not be built without losing the relationship.

What You Will Be Doing
Own the enhancement request pipeline across multiple strategic enterprise accounts at once. Build and maintain a structured system to track, prioritize, and respond to customer-sourced requirements, and keep requests moving rather than leaving them in “under consideration.”
Translate customer requirements into shipped products. Work at the level of customer pain, not just the feature that was asked for, and synthesize input from many accounts into a single, coherent product direction.
Turn input from strategic accounts into successful products. Look for patterns across accounts. Shape some of these patterns into formal partnerships for design. Make sure the resulting capabilities benefit the wider market, not just the single customer that made the request.
Feed validated customer patterns back into the core product roadmaps, influencing direction well beyond the accounts you cover.

Partner with product and engineering leads to write requirements they can act on without follow-up clarification meetings. Understand system architecture well enough to assess feasibility and scope on your own.
Operate across Product, Sales, Customer Success, and Legal. Support deal cycles as a product resource through RFP responses, security questionnaires, and roadmap presentations to prospects.
Navigate tension between a customer's contractual expectations and the internal roadmap , and tackle it directly rather than through routine escalation.
Create artifacts such as roadmap trackers, enhancement request dashboards, and decision memos that give customers and internal stakeholders visibility without requiring a meeting.
Advocate for customer needs inside the company while resisting the pull of the loudest or largest customer setting the roadmap at the expense of the broader market.

Extensive Experience: 7–10 years of product management experience, with at least 4 years in B2B enterprise software. A consistent record of owning a product area with meaningful revenue impact and of leading products from customer input through shipped, iterated outcomes. Direct experience working with named strategic accounts, not only through customer success proxies. Experience with hyperscalers, MSSPs and/or PubSec is a solid plus.

Structured Thinking and Bias for Closure: You bring order to unstructured problems, using data to prioritize and clear judgment when data is thin, and staying transparent about which is which. And it is a privileged surface for customers to discover, try, buy and expand through a seamless self-serve experience, connecting product usage, onboarding and growth in one place. It unites forces with GTM to automate acquisition, upsell, cross-sell and retention, with end-to-end ownership of the customer persona. The area is evolving fast.

What began as a self-serve growth surface (Station) is becoming the customer-facing window into Veriff's accuracy and fraud advantage for our largest enterprise customers.
The shape of this role
This is an IC-first leadership role, and the first genuine step into product leadership — distinct from a strong senior IC. At first you will lead through craft, authority and influence. You own the strategy, discovery, roadmap and delivery for your product area.
As you refine the strategic themes for this large product, we expect you to propose the team configuration needed to support our growth and company objectives. That will move you progressively from IC to manager, while retaining hands-on ownership of at least one part of the Customer Portal area in the mid-term. We will deliberately assess for both the IC craft bar and the latent management capability, because the role is designed to traverse the line.

Own the product strategy and roadmap for the Customer Portal area, tied explicitly to Veriff's commercial model and revenue drivers.
Run disciplined, continuous discovery with customers, and translate it into well-defined problem statements and a sequenced roadmap.
Make transparent prioritisation and trade-off calls across product ambition, technical sustainability and business urgency — especially where capability gaps mean we cannot do everything at once.
Define success metrics before building, and hold the team accountable to outcomes, not output.
Partner as a credible peer to Engineering, GTM, Fraud Ops and Design. Be the connective tissue that turns internal expertise into a customer-facing product.
Own launch as a discipline from the start — internal platform releases and external GTM — not a milestone at the end.
Set and uphold the product-craft bar. Mentor PMs and, in time, build and lead the team.
Champion AI internally, implementing new best practices for faster product discovery and delivery.

You are a product leader who has earned authority through the quality of your thinking rather than a title.
You have owned a product area end-to-end
From strategy through discovery, delivery and launch. You are equally comfortable in the messy front end of a problem and in the discipline of shipping.
You are looking for the step where your impact starts to come through others, and you are excited that this role begins as an individual leader and grows into managing a team — not the other way around.
You think commercially
You instinctively connect what you build to how the business grows, and you explain the “why” behind a product bet in terms of revenue, retention and customer trust, not just features and flows.
You run discovery as a continuous discipline
You get close to customers, including demanding enterprise accounts, and you can tell the difference between what they ask for and what they actually need.
You turn that into sharp problem statements and a phased roadmap where every step delivers a real customer outcome.
You prioritise ruthlessly and transparently

You define success before you build. When something goes wrong, you own it without deflection and change how you work as a result.
You lead through influence, not authority
You build credibility with engineering, go-to-market, design and operations partners as a genuine peer, and you reach good decisions with people who do not report to you.
You stay calm under uncertainty, create space for views that differ from your own, and commit gracefully once a call is made.
You raise the people around you

You are motivated by building and leading a team over time, with a realistic understanding that management is a different job — one focused on developing people and multiplying impact, not doing all the work yourself.
You stay current on your craft
You take pride in tracking how product management is evolving, and you consistently find time to experiment and fold what works into your practice.

Anyone can build AI insurance software now. The models are commoditized. The demos work. Almost nobody starts where Agency Revolution starts: thousands of independent P&C agencies already paying us to communicate with their clients, plus deep integrations into the systems where agency data actually lives.
The opportunity is the relationship layer — the system that notices when an agency's clients are at risk of churning, spots the cross-sell opportunity, picks the right message and channel and moment, and acts. We call it RelationshipOS. For ten years, agencies have trusted us to speak to their clients.

Now we're expanding what we can see: call transcripts, carrier communications, life events. The policies live in the agency's management system. The relationship lives with us. Nobody else has both the permission and the infrastructure.
We know what we're betting on. We don't yet know what makes an agency owner act on it. That's the job.
The strategic thesis is set. What's unresolved is whether it's true — whether an agency will actually change what they do because our system told them to, and what has to be built for that to happen. You're hired to answer that by shipping, not by studying.

s.h: Two halves, and you need both
s.t:
You personally build the bet. The intelligence layer is your work. Discovery with agency owners, prototypes in front of them within days, the smallest version that proves someone will act. Much of this is assembled rather than authored — the right vendor wired into AR Connect and pointed at a real use case will beat anything we could build from scratch this year. You don't hand this half to your team; it's too early and too ambiguous to delegate.
Your team drives the day-to-day execution and health of the existing platform. Two Product Owners and a Product Analyst keep a profitable, decade-old product healthy and improving. You set their priorities, strengthen their product judgment, raise their craft, and shield them from thrash. You remain the primary product manager responsible for the roadmap, discovery, and strategic product decisions. Done well, this is what buys you the time to do the first half.
Most people are good at one of these. We need someone who won't quietly abandon the other.
This position offers $125,000-$140,000 depending on experience and qualifications.

RelationshipOS — the intelligence layer. Churn signals. Cross-sell opportunities. Adaptive customer journeys instead of rigid sequences. You define what "acted on" means, instrument it, and are accountable for the number.
AR Connect and the vendor stack. AR Connect is our integration layer — where APIs pull in calls, carrier communications, life events, and other signals, and where third-party capability plugs into our distribution. It's the substrate the whole thesis sits on, and it's how a promising vendor becomes a live use case in front of agencies.
That work is yours: mapping the landscape of management systems, carrier connections, data enrichment providers, and AI vendors; deciding what we integrate versus build; running the POCs; and getting from "interesting demo" to something an agency actually uses. Data quality, latency, unit economics, and what happens when a vendor's model is wrong are your problems to surface early. You shape the deals and bring the recommendation — the SVP and our partnership team close them.
Voice AI as a channel. Not a feature — a real channel. Define the MVP, run pilots where AI handles outbound outreach with warm handoffs to agencies, and produce the evidence for whether this moves us from subscription toward outcome-based pricing.
The Agency Revolution roadmap. What ships, in what order, and what we stop doing. You own the sequencing and defend it.

Own the end-to-end strategy and roadmap for Canary's third-party integrations across reservation platforms, payment gateways, and other adjacent hospitality integrations.

Prioritize the integration roadmap based on customer demand, enterprise brand requirements, and revenue impact.
Own the relationships with integration partners including technical scoping, testing + certification, and managing each partnership across the integration lifecycle.
Partner with product teams to ensure integrations meet each product's needs while keeping the underlying platform consistent and maintainable.
Define and track integration health metrics - data accuracy, sync reliability, uptime, latency, and coverage - surfacing actionable improvements before customers feel the impact.
Represent the integrations roadmap to enterprise customers, sales, and customer success translating technical constraints into clear commitments and realistic timelines.

6+ years in product management, including experience owning platform, API, or integration products.

Experience managing external vendor and partner relationships, including technical scoping and certification processes.

Ability to operate with ambiguity and drive alignment across teams without direct authority.
Experience in hospitality technology (PMS, CRS, or payments) is a strong plus.

Die BWT Schweiz, bestehend aus den Unternehmen BWT AQUA AG und BWT AQUA Pharma \& Biotech AG, hat ihren Hauptsitz in Aesch BL und beschäftigt rund 500 Mitarbeitende. Beide Unternehmen sind Teil der BWT\-Gruppe. BWT ist Europas führendes Wasseraufbereitungsunternehmen mit mehr als 80 Tochter\- und Beteiligungsgesellschaften und über 6500 Mitarbeitenden weltweit.
BWT hat es sich zur Aufgabe gemacht, Wassertechnologien zu entwickeln, zu produzieren und zu vermarkten, die den Menschen eine bessere Lebensqualität bieten. Der Industrie werden ökonomisch sowie ökologisch sinnvolle Lösungen in der Wasseraufbereitung zur Verfügung gestellt.
Unser Portfolio an Technologien und Produkten deckt vom Wassereingang bis zum Verbraucher alle Bereiche der Wasseraufbereitung ab. In unseren Hauptbereichen Wasseraufbereitung für Industrie, Gewerbe und Private, Reinstwasser und Trinkwasserspender sorgen wir für perfektes Wasser im täglichen Leben. Abgerundet wird unser Angebot durch einen umfassenden Service.
Zur Verstärkung unseres Teams **im Produktmanagement in der BWT AQUA AG** suchen wir dich als:
**Produktmanager Ionenaustauscher \& Umkehrosmosenanlagen 100% (alle)**
***"Wir können alles \- ausser langweilig"***
**Diese spannenden und interessanten Aufgaben warten auf dich:**
* Du übernimmst die fachliche Verantwortung für das Produktportfolio Ionenaustauscher und Umkehrosmoseanlagen für die Anwendungsgebiete Trinkwasser, Gastronomie, Unternehmen und Spitäler, Gebäude und Industrie sowie Beleuchtungstechnik.
* Du managst und optimierst das Portfolio über den gesamten Lebenszyklus hinweg.
* Gemeinsam mit unserem Verkaufsteam entwickelst du verkaufsfördernde Massnahmen.
* Mit unserem Marketingteam erarbeitest du passgenaue Inhalte für die entsprechenden Kanäle.
* Du bist die kompetente Ansprechperson in deinem Verantwortungsbereich – für den Vertrieb, das Marketing und unsere Geschäftspartner.
**Diese Eigenschaften zeichnen dich aus:**
* Du hast eine technische Ausbildung oder ein Studium im Bereich Maschinenbau, Verfahrenstechnik, Elektromechanik oder in einer ähnlichen Fachrichtung und verfügst idealerweise bereits über entsprechende Berufserfahrung.
* Du verfügst über betriebswirtschaftliche und Marketingkenntnisse.
* Erfahrung in der Wasseraufbereitung und Verfahrenstechnik ist von Vorteil.
* Erfahrung im Produktmanagement oder im technischen Verkauf von Industriegütern ist von Vorteil.
* Du begeisterst dich für wassertechnische Produkte in einer zukunftsorientierten Branche.
* Du arbeitest selbstständig, zuverlässig und genau und bist gleichzeitig ein echter Teamplayer.
* Vertriebsorientiertes Denken und Handeln sind für dich selbstverständlich.
* Weiterbildungen im Produktmanagement sind ein Plus.
**Du bist und verfügst über:**
* Ausdauer, Kommunikationsstärke und die nötige Portion Durchsetzungsvermögen.
* Eine analytische und systematische Arbeitsweise mit einem klaren Blick für Lösungen Offenheit für Neues.
* Sehr gute Deutsch\- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift; Französischkenntnisse sind von Vorteil.
* Einen empathischen und wertschätzenden Umgang mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen.
**Unser Angebot**
Es erwartet Dich eine interessante und abwechslungsreiche Tätigkeit in einem lebhaften und kollegialen Arbeitsumfeld, welches Flexibilität und Selbstständigkeit erfordert. Du wirst dabei von einem erfahrenen und langjährigen Team unterstützt.
**Das sind wir:**
Die BWT AQUA AG hat eine flache Hierarchie und legt grossen Wert auf ein familiäres und angenehmes Zusammenarbeiten. Es besteht eine Du\-Kultur bis in die oberste Führungsebene. Dank unseren Werten dürfen wir auf viele langjährige Arbeitskolleginnen und Kollegen zählen.
**Ausserdem kannst du von weiteren Vorteilen profitieren:**
* Firmeneigene Kantine
* Jobticket (TNW Abo)
* Kostenlose Parkplätze
* Vergünstigungen aus dem BWT\-Aktikelsortiment
